tests.procedure: Under strong white light check each received sample container separately in a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, colour and conformity with the visual specification.

Weigh 100 mg in a stoppered tube; add 0.1 mL solvent, shake 1 min, hold at 25.0 ± 0.5 °C for 15 min, repeat shake/hold once if not dissolved; add 0.9 mL, then 2 mL, then 7 mL solvent with the same shake and hold steps to classify very soluble / freely soluble / soluble / sparingly soluble; if still undissolved use 10 mg in 10 mL (slightly soluble), then 1 mg in 10 mL (very slightly soluble), else practically insoluble. Repeat with the other solvent.

Identification test 1 (reactions of zinc) on a 100 mg/mL solution: (A) with sodium acetate, hydrogen sulfide gives a white precipitate insoluble in acetic acid but dissolved by 3 N hydrochloric acid; (B) ammonium sulfide TS gives a similar precipitate in neutral and alkaline solution; (C) potassium ferrocyanide TS gives a white precipitate insoluble in 3 N hydrochloric acid.

TLC identification: standard 10 mg/mL USP Potassium Gluconate RS; sample 10 mg/mL Zinc Gluconate (warm at 60 °C if needed). Silica gel 0.25 mm layer; apply 5 µL; develop with alcohol : ethyl acetate : ammonium hydroxide : water (50:10:10:30) to about three-quarters of the plate; dry at 110 °C 20 min; spray with ammonium molybdate / ceric sulfate reagent; heat at 110 °C about 10 min.

details.developingSolvent: alcohol : ethyl acetate : ammonium hydroxide : water 50:10:10:30
details.sprayReagent: 2.5 g ammonium molybdate in 50 mL 2 N sulfuric acid; add 1.0 g ceric sulfate; dilute with 2 N sulfuric acid to 100 mL

tests.procedure: Chloride limit test: sample 1.0 g dissolved in 30-40 mL water, neutralised with nitric acid to litmus if necessary; add 1 mL nitric acid and 1 mL silver nitrate TS, water to 50 mL; stand 5 min protected from direct sunlight; compare turbidity with the standard (0.7 mL of 0.020 N hydrochloric acid).

Sulfate limit test: sample 2.0 g dissolved in 30-40 mL water, neutralised with hydrochloric acid to litmus if necessary; add 1 mL 3 N hydrochloric acid, 3 mL barium chloride TS, water to 50 mL; stand 10 min; compare turbidity with the standard (1.0 mL of 0.020 N sulfuric acid).

Arsenic limit test (arsenic apparatus, procedure 1): test preparation 1 g in 35 mL water; standard 3.0 mL standard arsenic solution in 35 mL water; both treated with 20 mL 7 N sulfuric acid, potassium iodide TS, stannous chloride TS and isopropyl alcohol, stand 30 min; generate arsine with granular zinc through a lead-acetate cotton scrubber into silver diethyldithiocarbamate TS for 45 min at room temperature. Test colour must not exceed the standard.

details.reference: USP <211> Procedure 1; in-house method validation for arsenic
details.technique: arsenic apparatus (colour); spec sheet says arsenic apparatus / AAS (see openQuestions)

tests.procedure: Lead limit test by AAS: sample 1.0 g with 9 N hydrochloric acid, water, ascorbic acid-sodium iodide solution and trioctylphosphine oxide solution, shaken and separated; organic layer is the sample solution. Standard: organic layer containing 2 µg/mL lead (from lead nitrate stock). Blank: same reagents without sample. Atomic absorption at 283.3 nm, lead hollow-cathode lamp, air-acetylene flame. Sample absorbance must not exceed the standard absorbance.

details.systemSuitability: absorbance of the standard and blank significantly different

tests.procedure: Cadmium by AAS, standard addition: sample stock 10.0 g in 50 mL water; solution A = 5.0 mL stock to 25 mL (0 µg/mL added Cd), solution B = 5.0 mL stock + 2.0 mL Cd standard (12.5 µg/mL) to 25 mL (1.0 µg/mL added), solution C = 5.0 mL stock + 4.0 mL Cd standard to 25 mL (2.0 µg/mL added); blank water. Cadmium hollow-cathode lamp, 228.8 nm, air-acetylene flame; determine absorbances of A, B and C. The calculation of the cadmium result from the absorbances is not stated.

details.standardStock: 0.1372 mg/mL cadmium nitrate; standard 12.5 µg/mL Cd (25 mL stock to 100 mL with 1 mL HCl)

tests.heldBack: ICP method incomplete: calculation of the cadmium result from the absorbances of solutions A, B and C is not stated

tests.procedure: Reducing substances (residual titration): sample 1.0 g dissolved in 10 mL water in a 250 mL flask; add 25 mL alkaline cupric citrate TS, cover, boil gently 5 min (timed), cool rapidly; add 25 mL 0.6 N acetic acid, 10.0 mL 0.1 N iodine VS and 10 mL 3 N hydrochloric acid; titrate the excess iodine with 0.1 N sodium thiosulfate VS, adding starch TS near the endpoint; blank with 10 mL water. Result % (as dextrose) = [(VB - VS) x N x F / W] x 100, F = 27 mg/mEq.

details.titrant: 0.1 N iodine VS (residual), back titrant 0.1 N sodium thiosulfate VS
details.indicator: starch TS, 3 mL near the endpoint
details.formula: Result = [((VB - VS) x N x F) / W] x 100; VB = blank back titrant (mL), VS = sample back titrant (mL), N = back titrant normality (mEq/mL), F = 27 mg/mEq, W = sample weight (mg)

tests.procedure: pH: measure a 10 mg/mL solution of the sample with a calibrated pH meter.
Water determination: Karl Fischer titration of the sample with a calibrated Karl Fischer apparatus.

Assay (direct complexometric titration): sample 700 mg dissolved in 100 mL water; add 5 mL ammonia-ammonium chloride buffer TS and 0.1 mL Eriochrome black TS; titrate with 0.05 M edetate disodium VS to deep blue; blank 100 mL water. Result % = [(VS - VB) x M x F / W] x 100, F = 455.7 mg/mmol, W in mg.

details.titrantStandardization: about 200 mg chelometric standard calcium carbonate, dried at 210 °C for 4 h, dissolved with dilute hydrochloric acid, titrated with edetate disodium with hydroxy naphthol blue at pH 12-13; M = (gCaCO3 x Assay/100 x 1000) / (100.09 x mL EDTA)
details.formula: Result = [((VS - VB) x M x F) / W] x 100; VS = sample titrant (mL), VB = blank titrant (mL), M = titrant molarity (mmol/mL), F = 455.7 mg/mmol, W = sample weight (mg)
